thread.title: Broadcom: Lets See Share Reductions First - Broadcom Limited (NASDAQ:AVGO) | Seeking Alpha

author: Stone Fox Capital
title: Broadcom: Lets See Share Reductions First - Broadcom Limited (NASDAQ:AVGO) | Seeking Alpha
text:
After failing to acquire Qualcomm ( QCOM ) and facing market questions about the sustainability of the business model, Broadcom ( AVGO ) had one simple solution. The stock trades at a cheap valuation so the easy solution per my previous research is to buy itself to prove to the market that the company doesn't need to buy growth now that the market cap is above $100 billion.
Source: Broadcom website
Not Helping Anybody reviewing the FQ2 earnings report will quickly come to the concerning part of the business. Broadcom spends the whole report discussing massive margins and very little time talking about technology achievements. The market truly wonders if the semi company can thrive without buying the R&D of another firm and stripping out costs.
The opening segment from CEO Hock Tan on the earnings conference call was 950 words long and included not one mention of actual technology development or achievements. The CEO discussed the optical market or the data center cloud segment, but nothing about specific technologies.
Fo the quarter, Broadcom only spent $887 million on operating expenses with a similar forecast for the current quarter. The company is spending about $736 million on R&D and a very small $156 million on SG&A. Remember the revenue quarterly rate is $5 billion allowing the company to generate the incredible 48%+ operating margins.
In comparison to other chip giants like Intel ( INTC ) and Qualcomm, Broadcom spent a meager $3.3 billion on R&D last year. The margins wouldn't be so high, if the company was spending similar levels on development.
AVGO Research and Development Expense (Annual) data by YCharts
The stock is down following earnings partly due to some wireless industry related news of reduced orders from Apple ( AAPL ). The interesting part of the story is that Broadcom is hardly focused on wireless customers with the recent purchase of the storage related business from Brocade contributing to the Enterprise Storage division coming close to matching the Wireless division in size. The Wireless division only contributed 26% of revenues in the quarter.
Source: Broadcom FQ2 earnings report
Load Up If Broadcom can maintain technology leadership and grow revenues while maintaining these levels of margins, the company has one simple solution: buy their own shares hand over fist.
The company announced the $12 billion repurchase plan back in early April. The initial signs are that the company is backing this plan with confidence. The worst possible outcome for shareholders is for Broadcom to spend over $10 billion on share buybacks to only face a 2019 or 2020 story where the company is broken due to the lack of investments in technology.
For FQ1 that ended in April, Broadcom repurchased 1.5 million shares for $347 million. Another 4.9 million shares were bought for $1,155 million by June 1. These numbers will show up in the FQ3 diluted share count.
The company ended April with $8.2 billion in cash but has $17.6 billion in debt leaving net debt of $9.4 billion. Broadcom will need substantial conviction to repurchase shares while in a net debt position.
Free cash flow was $2.1 billion in the last quarter for over 40% of revenues so the company can repurchase several billion worth of shares in a quarter without altering the net debt position.
Broadcom regularly issues share via either acquisitions or stock options so the share count has historically risen. The company ended FQ2 with 460 million shares outstanding and the forecast was for the share count to only dip to 457 million shares.
AVGO Stock Buybacks (Quarterly) data by YCharts
The company has already repurchased 6.4 million shares basically in April and May. A key dynamic for the FQ3 report is for the average share count to fall by more than 3 million shares.
The big part of the story is whether Broadcom can reduce the share count in a meaningful way. The EPS target for next fiscal year is only $20.20 that amounts to meager 3.5% growth rate. The combination of mid-single digits organic revenue growth and a 5% reduction to shares outstanding should boost EPS by far in excess of this analyst target.
AVGO EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that Broadcom needs to convince the market that the business model can evolve beyond acquiring companies and the related technology. A massive share buyback is a big way to boost earnings and for the company to show that the current business lines and tight cost controls can sustain profit margins and hence cash flows.
The management team needs to invest in itself wisely. My doubts still exist that Broadcom can spend at these reduced levels and not eventually lose technology mind share. The company needs to convince us more via actual share count reductions keeping us on the sidelines as the stock trades in a range between $220 and $280.
Disclosure: I am/we are long AAPL.
